title: AI moderation with human override
description:
As a publication admin, I want an AI moderator to review content against the rules with a human able to override, so that moderation scales.

Notes: the AI returns a decision (allow, hide, escalate), a short rationale and a confidence. Low confidence escalates to the human queue. Human overrides are recorded and become labelled examples (can feed Cyclotron feedback, see PPY-77bb3b milestone 5). Default model for language-model tasks: GPT-6 Luna unless stated otherwise; any other model needs explicit approval.

```gherkin
Feature: AI moderation
  Scenario: Confident allow
    When the AI moderator allows an item with high confidence
    Then the item stays public and the decision and rationale are recorded

  Scenario: Hide
    When the AI moderator decides to hide an item
    Then it is hidden and the author may see the reason

  Scenario: Escalate
    When confidence is below the threshold
    Then the item goes to the human queue

  Scenario: Human override
    When a moderator reverses an AI decision
    Then the reversal is recorded as an override with the moderator's identity
```

comments.author: home
comments.text: Built: moderation.mode ai. A worker asks GPT-6 Luna (stubbed in tests) to allow or hide each new item, applies it as a logged action marked by ai, and a human decision always stands. Key in SSM SecureString /papyrus/<site>/openai-api-key; prompt in a file.
